title: Pinole/Hercules Water Pollution Control Plant, Pinole, California
source: HDR for the City of Pinole, Pinole/Hercules WPCP Project, Technical Memorandum 15 - Hydraulic Profile, March 1, 2013 (preliminary, public record)
strip: This analysis assumes the existing secondary clarifier weirs will be reinstalled, and the invert elevation raised 1.5-in to 109.3-ft\.
The new distribution box will consist of five weirs\.

question: Under the new NPDES permit all influent up to the 20 mgd peak wet weather flow (with 10 mgd RAS in contact stabilization mode) must receive secondary treatment. Today the secondary system passes only about 11 mgd. Using the hydraulic profile (Figure 15-3) and the hydraulic element list, can the upgraded plant pass ADWF, MMF, MDF and 20 mgd PWWF with at least 1 ft of freeboard at every unit? Which structures limit flow or carry the largest headloss, at what flow, and what modifications to the existing primary, aeration-basin, secondary-clarifier and disinfection hydraulics are needed?
exclude_reason: Design check of an already-proposed upgrade: the fixes and modelled water surfaces are in the input element lists, so a blind score would be meaningless. Kept as a second profile drawing for demos.
